extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys before the USPTO, respondents in OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving a USPTO OED disciplinary complaint by settlement, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions (suspension), conditions for limited practice and reinstatement, and procedural mechanisms for enforcement and publication. Targets practitioner conduct before the Office and post-order compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) by engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order is based on admitted misrepresentations to a client (providing fictitious filing dates, fabricated application numbers, and altered USPTO documents) rather than seeking assistance when overwhelmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct: neglect of matters entrusted (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by neglecting matters entrusted to him (failing to file multiple patent applications as instructed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect may include failure to file applications for which a client provided instructions; such neglect forms a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement Agreement satisfies 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolving all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement under § 11.26 must include stipulated facts and legal conclusions and result in a Final Order approved by the USPTO Director or designate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension sanction (24 months) and commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the duration and start date of suspension as the effective sanction for the admitted violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 imposes duties and procedures a suspended practitioner must follow (e.g., client notification and record handling) and compliance is a condition of the suspension terms and any future reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice for narrow purpose (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limited recognition is strictly time-limited and only to enable compliance with specific regulatory duties (e.g., wrap-up obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates; Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs administrative steps to prevent suspended practitioners from accessing USPTO systems and filing under prior credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining new customer number or PKI while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents circumventing the dissociation by obtaining new credentials during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c) and § 11.7 standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must show, to the satisfaction of the OED Director as required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c), that: (1) Respondent has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission; (2) the resumption of Respondent's practice before the Office will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; and (3) Respondent has complied with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the full period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires both character/competence showings and proof of compliance with duties during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limitation on filing for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not file a request for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 during the first ninety (90) days from the date the Final Order is signed, but may file any time after ninety (90) days from that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order creates a minimum period before a reinstatement petition may be filed (90 days), even though the full suspension is 24 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director authority to issue Order to Show Cause for noncompliance during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the twenty-four (24) month period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall: (1) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause and (2) send it to Respondent's last address of record and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause process may lead to amendments to the Final Order (e.g., delaying eligibility to request reinstatement) or immediate suspension of any stayed remaining suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences following Order to Show Cause and OED Director recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: After consideration of Respondent's response to an Order to Show Cause, the OED Director may deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response, and evidence to the USPTO Director and request that the Director amend the Final Order or lift the stay of any remaining suspension and immediately suspend Respondent for all or part of the remaining period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the escalation path and possible remedies (amendment of reinstatement eligibility or immediate suspension) if noncompliance is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: If suspended pursuant to subparagraph L: additional notice and dissociation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended pursuant to the OED Director's action under subparagraph L, then: (1) Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; (2) the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; (3) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; (4) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated; and (5) Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the OED Director invokes additional suspension measures, the same administrative safeguards and public notice requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on OED Director actions under subparagraph L during the 24-month period
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or the Final Order shall limit the number of times the OED Director or the USPTO Director may act pursuant to the provisions of subparagraph L for acts and/or omissions occurring during the twenty-four (24) month period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director may repeatedly pursue Orders to Show Cause or related actions for misconduct during the suspension window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are publicly posted and notices are distributed to relevant state agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Notice of Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Suspension describes the practitioner's registration number, the length of suspension, the rules violated (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) and § 10.77(c)), the eligibility conditions for reinstatement (eligible after 90 days subject to conditions), and a short narrative of the misconduct and remorse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice included in the Final Order illustrates the disclosure content and tone required for Official Gazette publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of disciplinary proceeding to be considered in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the Office's attention, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as (a) an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior Final Order may be used to aggravate sanctions or counter favorable assertions in later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not impose payment of costs from one party to the other.
